title: Rails 8 app scaffold with PostgreSQL
description: Run `rails new . --force --database=postgresql --css=tailwind --skip-jbuilder --skip-test` inside /Users/michael/Projects/flip7-app (keep CLAUDE.md, README.md, app_spec.txt, docs/, features.json, .gitignore intact — merge with existing files). Install default gems. Verify with `bin/rails -v` and `bin/rails runner 'puts Rails.version'`. Acceptance criteria: (1) Gemfile exists and includes rails ~> 8.1, (2) bin/rails boots without error, (3) config/database.yml uses postgresql adapter, (4) app/, config/, db/ directories created.
notes: Done 2026-04-14. Worker committed be2e076 (102 files). Rails 8.1.3 + Postgres + Tailwind. Note: eslint.config.js added to satisfy global pre-commit hook — ignores all Rails-generated JS.

title: Add core gems to Gemfile and bundle install
description: Add to Gemfile: devise, omniauth, omniauth-google-oauth2, omniauth-rails_csrf_protection, sidekiq, redis, aasm, phlex-rails, with_advisory_lock, rspec-rails (development/test group), factory_bot_rails (dev/test), faker (dev/test). Run `bundle install`. Acceptance criteria: (1) Gemfile has all listed gems, (2) bundle install succeeds, (3) `bundle exec rails -v` still works.
notes: Done 2026-04-14. Worker committed e7fb3bf. 12 gems added: devise, omniauth, omniauth-google-oauth2, omniauth-rails_csrf_protection, sidekiq, redis, aasm, phlex-rails, with_advisory_lock, rspec-rails, factory_bot_rails, faker. 152 gems total after bundle install.

title: Install RSpec + FactoryBot
description: Run `bin/rails generate rspec:install`. Configure FactoryBot in spec/rails_helper.rb. Create spec/factories/.keep. Acceptance criteria: (1) spec/rails_helper.rb exists, (2) spec/spec_helper.rb exists, (3) `bundle exec rspec --version` works, (4) an empty `bundle exec rspec` run reports 0 examples without error.

title: Create development and test databases
description: Update config/database.yml if needed (use localhost/unix socket for dev). Run `bin/rails db:create`. If Postgres isn't running locally, note this in the return and mark success:false with a hint (workers after this feature can assume dev DB exists). Acceptance criteria: (1) `bin/rails db:version` works without error in both development and test.

title: User model with Devise + OmniAuth + game stats
description: Create the User model per docs/data_model.md §users. Generate Devise install, generate User model with `bin/rails generate devise User`, then edit the migration to add all columns from data_model.md (provider, uid, name, avatar_url, elo_rating, games_played, games_won, total_rounds_played, total_flip7s, highest_round_score, ranked_wins, ranked_losses, current_win_streak, best_win_streak). Add `from_omniauth` class method to User model per docs/realtime.md §Authentication. Run migration. Write a simple RSpec model spec covering validations and `from_omniauth`. Acceptance criteria: (1) `bin/rails db:migrate` succeeds, (2) `User.new.valid?` works, (3) `bundle exec rspec spec/models/user_spec.rb` passes, (4) `User.from_omniauth` creates a user from an OpenStruct mock.

title: Google OAuth config and callback controller
description: Configure omniauth-google-oauth2 in config/initializers/devise.rb using Rails credentials (placeholder GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET). Create OmniauthCallbacksController at app/controllers/users/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb with `google_oauth2` action calling `User.from_omniauth`. Update routes. Write request spec for the callback with a mock auth hash. Acceptance criteria: (1) routes include `/users/auth/google_oauth2/callback`, (2) callback controller exists, (3) request spec passes with a mocked auth hash.

title: Tailwind + DaisyUI 5 setup
description: Install DaisyUI as a Tailwind plugin (DaisyUI 5). Configure tailwind.config.js (or equivalent Rails 8 config) to include the daisyui plugin with themes: dark (default), light, cyberpunk, retro, dracula, night. Verify by rendering a DaisyUI button component in the default landing view. Acceptance criteria: (1) DaisyUI classes (like `btn btn-primary`) render with DaisyUI styling, (2) theme switching via `data-theme` attribute works, (3) `bin/rails assets:precompile` succeeds.

title: Landing page with play options
description: Create PagesController with `home` action. Route root to it. Build the landing view with a hero section, three CTA buttons (Play Solo, Join Casual, Ranked Duel), and a Devise sign-in-with-Google link. Use DaisyUI components. Request spec: GET / returns 200 and includes 'Flip 7' and 'Play Solo'. Acceptance criteria: (1) GET / returns 200, (2) response body includes the three CTAs, (3) request spec passes.

title: Profile page with user stats
description: Create ProfilesController with `show` action at route `/profile` (own) and `/profile/:id` (public). Display: name, avatar_url, elo_rating, games_played, games_won, total_flip7s, highest_round_score. Require auth for `/profile`, public for `/profile/:id`. Acceptance criteria: (1) unauthenticated GET /profile redirects to sign-in, (2) authenticated GET /profile shows stats, (3) GET /profile/:id works for any user, (4) request spec passes.

title: Game, GamePlayer, MatchResult models
description: Create migrations and models for games, game_players, match_results per docs/data_model.md. Use jsonb columns as specified. Include AASM setup on Game (states: waiting, in_progress, completed, abandoned, expired) per docs/game_engine.md. Add associations. Write factories and model specs for each. Acceptance criteria: (1) migrations run cleanly, (2) `Game.new.valid?` works, (3) AASM state machine transitions work, (4) model specs pass.

title: GameEngine service — full game logic
description: Implement app/services/game_engine.rb per docs/game_engine.md. Include: start_round, hit, stay, resolve_action, check_round_end, score_round, check_game_end, timeout_turn, validate_turn, draw_card, check_bust, bust_probability. Implement deck generation (94 cards × deck_count, pyramid distribution, action cards, modifiers). Implement full reshuffle at round start. Write exhaustive RSpec service spec covering the critical test cases from app_spec.txt §14 (drawing each card type, bust detection, Second Chance saves, Flip 7 detection, scoring order, action cards, multi-deck). Acceptance criteria: (1) all spec/services/game_engine_spec.rb examples pass, (2) covers at least 20 distinct test cases including multi-deck and full reshuffle.

title: BotBrain with conservative/balanced/aggressive strategies
description: Implement app/services/bot_brain.rb per docs/game_engine.md §Simulation Engine. Implement conservative, balanced, and aggressive strategies (NOT optimal — that's Phase 7). Include choose_action_target with strategy-specific targeting logic. Write service spec covering decide() for each strategy given various hand states. Acceptance criteria: (1) BotBrain.new(strategy:, game_state:, player_id:).decide returns :hit or :stay, (2) each strategy produces measurably different outputs on the same inputs, (3) spec passes.

title: Solo game controller + views
description: Create GamesController (new, create, show) and MovesController (hit, stay, target) per app_spec.txt §12. Solo setup page at /play/solo (bot count 1-9, difficulty per bot). POST /games creates a solo Game with bot GamePlayers. GET /games/:id renders the game board. Basic HTML (Hotwire enhancements come later). BotTurnJob fires after each human turn in solo mode to advance bot turns. Acceptance criteria: (1) full solo game can be played from creation to round completion via request specs, (2) bot players take turns automatically, (3) round scoring matches GameEngine output.

title: Card flip animation + card_flip Stimulus controller
description: Add the CSS from docs/frontend.md §Card Flip Animation to the stylesheet. Create app/javascript/controllers/card_flip_controller.js (15-40 lines) that toggles the `.flipped` class on elements with `data-controller='card-flip'`. Render cards in views using the card partial with data attributes. Acceptance criteria: (1) app/assets/stylesheets contains the card flip CSS, (2) card_flip_controller.js exists and toggles class on connect or click, (3) visual verification: a test page shows a card flipping on click.

title: Mobile-responsive game board layout
description: Apply DaisyUI + Tailwind mobile-first breakpoints to the game view per docs/frontend.md §Mobile Responsiveness. Hit/Stay buttons bottom-anchored (thumb-reachable, min 44px touch target). Cards in horizontal scroll on mobile, grid on desktop. Sticky turn timer top bar. Acceptance criteria: (1) game view renders correctly at mobile (375px), tablet (768px), and desktop (1280px) widths, (2) Hit/Stay buttons are always accessible.

title: Achievement model + seed data (32 achievements)
description: Create Achievement and UserAchievement models + migrations per docs/data_model.md. Write db/seeds/achievements.yml with all 32 entries from docs/achievements.md (20 regular + 12 anti). Add a seed loader that idempotently upserts achievements from YAML. Run `bin/rails db:seed`. Acceptance criteria: (1) 32 achievements in the database after seeding, (2) running seed twice does not duplicate, (3) Achievement.where(is_anti: true).count == 12.

title: AchievementEvaluator service
description: Implement app/services/achievement_evaluator.rb that takes a game, a user, and round results, and checks all 32 achievements for eligibility. For tiered achievements (flip7_*), increment progress and unlock when tier_target is met. Creates/updates UserAchievement records. Acceptance criteria: (1) unit spec covers at least 10 distinct achievement unlock scenarios, (2) tiered progression works (flip7_first → flip7_5 → ...), (3) idempotent — evaluating the same state twice does not double-unlock.

title: Achievement display on profile page
description: Update ProfilesController#show to load user achievements grouped by category and rarity. Render a grid of unlocked + locked achievements with icons and tooltips. Show progress bars for tiered achievements. Acceptance criteria: (1) profile page shows all 32 achievements (unlocked highlighted, locked dimmed), (2) tiered progress bars show current/target, (3) category tabs work.

title: Action Cable + Redis adapter setup
description: Configure config/cable.yml to use redis adapter. Set REDIS_URL env var handling. Create ApplicationCable::Connection with current_user authentication via warden (Devise). Write a basic channels_spec to verify subscription works. Acceptance criteria: (1) cable.yml uses redis in dev and prod, (2) ApplicationCable::Connection authenticates via Devise, (3) a test subscription to a dummy channel succeeds.

title: Sidekiq setup + Redis connection
description: Configure Sidekiq as the ActiveJob queue adapter. Mount Sidekiq web UI at /sidekiq (protected by Devise admin later). Verify a trivial job can be enqueued and processed. Acceptance criteria: (1) config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq, (2) bundle exec sidekiq boots without error, (3) a TestJob runs successfully.

title: GameChannel with state sync and disconnect handling
description: Implement app/channels/game_channel.rb per docs/realtime.md. On subscribe: send full state_sync for reconnect scenarios. On unsubscribe: enqueue PlayerDisconnectJob with 30s delay. Acceptance criteria: (1) channel spec subscribes successfully, (2) state_sync broadcast contains full HTML, (3) PlayerDisconnectJob is enqueued on unsubscribe.

title: Room code generation + casual join flow
description: Implement 4-char room code generation (A-H, J-N, P-Z, 2-9; excludes I/O/0/1) with offensive word blocklist. Add RoomExpiryJob (5min). Build /play/casual (host creates room), /join (code entry), /join/:code (direct join). Host-starts-game flow. Acceptance criteria: (1) unique room codes, (2) expired rooms marked via Sidekiq cron, (3) full host→join→start flow passes request specs.

title: Lobby UI with Turbo Stream player presence
description: Render the lobby partial for games in waiting state. Subscribe to LobbyChannel for real-time player-joined broadcasts. Show avatars, allow host to add bots, show deck count (2 decks when 11+ players). Acceptance criteria: (1) lobby updates in real-time as players join (verified via Action Cable test), (2) host sees Start Game button, non-hosts don't, (3) deck count badge appears at 11+ players.

title: Real-time game broadcasts via Turbo Streams
description: Wire the GameEngine's event output to Turbo Stream broadcasts on GameChannel. On each move (hit/stay/target), broadcast HTML fragments to all subscribers. Acceptance criteria: (1) a move made by player A is visible to player B via Action Cable within 200ms in tests, (2) card reveal, stay status, bust animation, action resolution all broadcast correctly, (3) no dual update paths — only Turbo Streams drive UI state during gameplay.

title: Turn timer — Sidekiq enforced + client-side Stimulus countdown
description: Implement TurnTimeoutJob with turn_number staleness guard. On turn start, update game.turn_expires_at and enqueue the job with 10s delay. Create timer_controller.js to render a countdown bar from the absolute timestamp. Expiry triggers auto-Stay server-side. Acceptance criteria: (1) TurnTimeoutJob ignores stale turn_number values, (2) auto-Stay fires exactly once per turn even with rapid actions, (3) client countdown bar matches server expiry within 1 second.

title: Reconnection handling with 30s grace period
description: On unsubscribe: PlayerDisconnectJob enqueued with 30s wait. On reconnect (new subscribe): cancel the pending job, send state_sync. If job fires: mark player as disconnected, forfeit ranked game or auto-Stay casual game. Acceptance criteria: (1) reconnect within 30s resumes gameplay, (2) reconnect after 30s shows forfeit screen, (3) job handles the race condition where reconnect and job fire simultaneously.

title: EloCalculator service
description: Implement app/services/elo_calculator.rb per docs/realtime.md §Elo System. Formula: `new_rating = current + K * (actual - expected)` with K=48 for first 20 games, K=32 after. Elo floor 100. Returns new_rating for both players. Acceptance criteria: (1) unit spec with 10+ scenarios (underdog wins, favorite wins, provisional vs established), (2) floor is enforced, (3) result is deterministic for same inputs.

title: Matchmaking — Redis queue + expanding Elo range worker
description: Implement MatchmakingChannel, MatchmakingWorkerJob (runs every 5s via sidekiq-cron), and the expanding range algorithm (0s: ±50, 10s: ±100, 20s: ±200, 30s: ±500, 60s: any). Use Redis sorted set keyed by Elo. On match found, create a Game and broadcast to both players via MatchmakingChannel. Acceptance criteria: (1) two players in queue within Elo range get matched within 15s in tests, (2) expanding range works over time, (3) cancelled queue entries are removed from Redis.

title: Ranked game flow (2-player, Elo update on completion)
description: Create /play/ranked page that enters matchmaking queue. Require 5+ casual games before ranked unlocks. On game completion for ranked mode, update both players' Elo via EloCalculator and record MatchResult with elo_before/after/change. Acceptance criteria: (1) ranked game cannot start with <5 casual games played, (2) Elo updates correctly on game end, (3) MatchResult records include Elo delta.

title: Leaderboard page (ranked Elo)
description: GET /leaderboard shows top 100 users by elo_rating. Include games_played, win_rate, and user avatar. Paginated. Cached for 5 minutes. Acceptance criteria: (1) page shows users ordered by elo DESC, (2) pagination works, (3) cache invalidates on game completion.

title: Friendships model + friends list UI
description: Create Friendship model per docs/data_model.md. FriendsController with index (list friends + pending requests), create (send request), accept, destroy, challenge (create ranked game invite). Acceptance criteria: (1) friend request flow works end-to-end, (2) bidirectional lookups use the index on friend_id, (3) cannot friend self, (4) duplicate requests merge.

title: Rematch button (post-game one-click replay)
description: POST /games/:id/rematch creates a new Game with the same players and settings, linking via rematch_of column. Show Rematch button on completed game view. Acceptance criteria: (1) rematch creates new game with same players, (2) rematch_of references the previous game, (3) both players get notified via Action Cable (if multiplayer).

title: Stats dashboard (history, card frequency, trends)
description: GET /stats shows personal dashboard. /stats/history: paginated MatchResult list. /stats/cards: most drawn / most busted on. /stats/trends: Elo line chart + win rate over time. Use Chart.js or Chartkick via Stimulus. Acceptance criteria: (1) all four routes render, (2) charts render on valid data, (3) empty state handled.

title: Optimal bot strategy — port simulation engine
description: Port the TypeScript simulation engine from /Users/michael/Projects/flip7-simulations to Ruby as an extension of BotBrain's optimal strategy. Read the TS code to understand the probability calculations. Implement bust_probability and expected_value_of_hitting in Ruby. Acceptance criteria: (1) optimal bot outperforms balanced bot in 100-game simulation (spec runs this), (2) bust_probability calculations match TS reference outputs for 5 known hand states.

title: Interactive rules / tutorial page
description: GET /rules shows an interactive walkthrough of Flip7 rules with animated examples (card flip, bust, Flip 7, action cards). Use Stimulus controllers to drive the animations. Acceptance criteria: (1) page covers all rules from app_spec.txt §1, (2) interactive card flip demo works, (3) responsive on mobile.

title: SEO metadata + OpenGraph tags
description: Add meta description, OpenGraph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image), Twitter Card tags to layout. Create a static og:image for the landing page. Acceptance criteria: (1) layout includes meta tags, (2) landing page has unique og:title and og:description, (3) sharing a link on Slack/Twitter produces a preview.

title: Railway deployment config + Procfile
description: Create Procfile per docs/frontend.md §Deployment. Add production env var documentation to README. Add a railway.toml or equivalent if needed. Do NOT actually deploy — just get the config files in place for the human to push. Acceptance criteria: (1) Procfile exists with web, worker, release lines, (2) README documents all required env vars, (3) bin/rails assets:precompile succeeds locally.
